parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain the differences between using a compiler and an interpreter for:

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: the translation of a high-level language program,

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: the execution of a high-level language program.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: One phase of compilation is the code generation phase.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Name the two phases that are carried out before code generation.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Describe the code generation phase.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
It is necessary to find and output all the records in the transaction file which relate to a worker
with ID number 23714.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Describe how the file can be searched serially for all records with ID number 23714.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Explain how the serial search would differ if it was known that there was only one record
with that ID number.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Describe a more efficient search algorithm if the file is in numerical order of ID numbers.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The following ID numbers are to be sorted into numerical order, with the smallest first.
36721, 53967, 24378, 47869, 47691
Describe an algorithm for implementing an insertion sort on the above data.

text: A company uses a computerised payroll system. Details of the work done by employees each
week are stored serially in a transaction file. This transaction file is used to create the payroll at
the end of the week. It has to be sorted into the same order as the master file.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
State two types of sensor which would be needed to provide input to the robot, explaining
why each is necessary.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Discuss the use of robots in the car factory.

text: Robots are used to carry car bodies around in a car factory. They move from position to position
in a specific order so that the car parts can be added.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain how flat files differ from a relational database.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe three advantages of using a relational database rather than flat files to store
information.

text: A new school is being built on a single site. The computers will be networked with a central
storage facility.
Discuss different topologies and the media available for transmitting data around the network. [6]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe the difference between the use of pages and the use of segmentation in managing
memory.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A job is split by the operating system into a number of pages. At any one time, only some of
the pages are in memory.
Explain how the operating system keeps track of the different pages and the part played by
virtual memory in their movement.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Explain how the introduction of computing technology to a factory production line has
changed the working patterns of people who work there.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the expected changes in quality of work that can be expected.

text: State what is stored in each of the following special purpose registers in a computer and explain
how the contents are altered during the fetch/execute cycle.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why the response times in these two systems will be different.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the hardware, software and data structures of the two systems.

text: A shop uses two computer systems.
System 1
At the checkout, goods being bought are identified by the system. Details are given to the
customer along with the total amount owed.
System 2
Each evening details of the sales during the day are collected together. They are then used to
update the stock file.

number of digits (including none).
